missions.title: The Bike Lane Budget
missions.subtitle: Rates, Percents and a Planning Decision
missions.summary: The fictional city of Harlow can fund one protected bike lane. Listen to a planning meeting, read a memo, a cost table and a chart, compare the streets with percents and rates, then explain and write a recommendation.

missions.title: The Harbor Petition
missions.subtitle: Civic Research at the Waterfront
missions.summary: Neighbors in the fictional Baltimore harbor community of Brewer's Wharf have petitioned against a 640-space garage on the last open shoreline lot. Listen to the public hearing, read the petition and survey, choose more evidence, and argue for a plan.

missions.title: Lighthouse Letters
missions.subtitle: Perspective and Theme in Two Texts
missions.summary: A museum has received a keeper's letter, his daughter's diary and a newspaper report about the same 1938 storm. Listen, read, compare two narrators' perspectives, retell the night, and write about a shared theme.

missions.title: School Newsroom: The Cafeteria Debate
missions.subtitle: Civic Journalism & Policy Analysis
missions.summary: Our middle school throws away about 120 pounds of food each day while students ask for fresher lunch choices. Interview the head chef, analyze waste and cost data, choose your next lead, record a balanced broadcast, and publish an editorial for the school board.

missions.title: Saving the School Garden
missions.subtitle: Use evidence to help a community garden grow
missions.summary: The school garden dries out during warm weeks. Listen to the garden team, read two kinds of evidence, choose a fair next step, explain your plan aloud, and write a recommendation for the principal.

missions.title: Shade for Outdoor Learning
missions.subtitle: Use observations and test results to improve a sunny school courtyard
missions.summary: The class wants to learn outside, but the courtyard becomes hot. Listen to student observations, read a short science note, compare shade-test results, and recommend a careful first step.

missions.title: Space Colony Ecosystem Architect
missions.subtitle: Bio-Regenerative Life Support Mission
missions.summary: On Lunar Habitat Base Artemis, carbon dioxide is rising unexpectedly in Biodome 3 while the wheat makes less oxygen. Listen to telemetry, analyze the overnight log, choose which hypothesis to test, brief the commander, and write engineering orders.

missions.title: The Urban Watershed Mystery
missions.subtitle: Environmental Science Investigation
missions.summary: Fish populations in Riverdale Creek dropped sharply after spring storms. Investigate the runoff sources, analyze water chemistry data, choose your next lead, brief the City Council, and write an evidence-based remediation plan.

missions.title: A Welcoming Reading Nook
missions.subtitle: Use student observations and a class survey to plan a shared reading space
missions.summary: The library wants a small reading nook that works for different readers. Listen to student ideas, read about welcoming shared spaces, examine a survey, and recommend a careful first setup.
